title: Sharing a course with participants: ideas from other products
intro: This page covers Share with participants and the Learner Portal inside Semester, then Courses. It looks at how other products move a course from setup to learner access, and make the first visit useful. The examples come from the design reference libraries Mobbin and Refero. Group assignment belongs to report 04, reports to 08, and announcements and material delivery to 09. The screenshots were collected for this research. They do not prove what each product can do today.

questions.title: How do products publish a course: one switch, per-item visibility, or a scheduled release?
questions.answer: These screenshots show publication as more than one switch. Teachable has per-lesson 'Publish' controls and a 'Drip' panel timed in days after enrolment. Kajabi's module menu offers 'Draft', 'Publish', 'Drip' and 'Lock', then shows a 'Published' result. Podia separates 'Published', 'Open' and 'Visible', and shows a delayed module. Circle explains 'Open', 'Private' and 'Secret' audiences. For Essentials, keep course publication, who can see it, and when each item releases as separate, readable choices. The screenshots do not show what happens if you unpublish a course that is already active.

questions.title: How do products grant access (enrolled groups, link, code, or email), and how do they show permission levels?
questions.answer: Grant access from inside the course. Circle shows invitations with selected-space access and admin or moderator controls. Figma combines email invitations, 'Copy link' and visible permissions. A second Figma screen adds 'Anyone' access, 'View'/'Edit' and password protection. Notion names a 'Member' role in an email invitation. These are access patterns, not a learner role model to copy. A password is not evidence of a classroom join-code workflow. Enrolled-group inheritance and class codes are not shown in this set. Podia makes a 30-day trial limit explicit before inviting a customer. Gumroad is an example of what not to do on the creator side: 'Share' and 'Collaborators' navigation do not show a learner-access workflow.

questions.title: Can instructors preview the course as a learner, and how complete is that preview?
questions.answer: Preview means different things in different products. Circle explicitly labels preview as an enrolled member and keeps lesson content and a completion action. Canva places 'View as learner' beside the course editor. Teachable shows curriculum preview without proving the same role simulation. SchoolAI previews an AI activity as a student, which is narrower than a whole course portal. For Essentials, label the simulated learner and group. Confirm separately whether release dates, prerequisites and progress saves are simulated. The screenshots do not show those behaviours.

questions.title: What does the learner see first on the course home (next session, progress, materials, announcements)?
questions.answer: Day one needs a clear next action. Teachable shows 'Start Lesson', the lesson list and 0% completion. Coursera puts 'Continue learning', progress, 'Resume' and a weekly goal first. Circle provides community context and content entry points. For simulation education, adapt the next-action pattern to the next scheduled session and required preparation. These screenshots do not show a session-first portal. Treat announcements as context from module 09, and recordings and reports as a hand-off to 08.

questions.title: How does the instructor see that sharing worked (who opened it, pending invites)?
questions.answer: Publishing, inviting, joining and learning are different events. Podia shows 'Customer invited' alongside audience rows and progress. That supports an action confirmation and participation context, not evidence that an email was opened. Slack shows 'Pending' and 'Accepted' tabs plus bounced, resent and revoked invitation states. 'Pending' does not prove delivery. For Essentials, show the recipient, current access and available recovery action. Then distinguish invitation status from first course access and learning progress. No screenshot in this set shows a course-open event. Canva confirms the course is ready, reports team notification and offers 'Classwork' and 'Copy link'. It does not list learner acceptance.

questions.title: How similar is the course portal on web and on mobile?
questions.answer: Only Coursera has a matched web and iOS course-home pair in this set: Coursera's web home and Coursera's iOS home. Both show progress and the next learning action. Goals and navigation adapt to the device. The iOS 'Download' button shows an available action, not proven offline behaviour. Udemy is mobile context without a matched web screenshot. Teachable is a learner-facing preview inside an admin shell, not an ordinary learner session, and no matched mobile screenshot was kept. Keep shared learner progress and the next action across devices, but check invitation entry, sign-in and session joining separately.

references.title: Publishing a course space
references.question: Q1
references.take: Circle's publishing flow shows draft mode and 'Open'/'Private'/'Secret' audience descriptions, then topics, a thumbnail and 'Save changes'. 'Open' means community members, not the public internet.

references.title: Publishing course content
references.question: Q1
references.take: Kajabi's module menu offers 'Draft', 'Publish', 'Drip' and 'Lock'. Choosing 'Publish' produces a 'Published' result and a short confirmation message.

references.title: Publishing a course
references.question: Q1
references.take: Podia confirms 'Course published', separates 'Published'/'Open'/'Visible', and shows a delayed module plus an audience table with progress, signup, start and expiry columns.

references.title: Course publish settings
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable places per-lesson 'Publish' actions beside a 'Drip' panel with days after enrolment, 'Activate drip', notification controls and saved feedback.

references.title: Course visibility controls
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable's curriculum combines 'Preview' and per-lesson 'Publish' controls with a 'Drip' panel that visibly requires a plan upgrade.

references.title: Course release timing controls
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable's 'Drip' panel shows days after enrolment, a numeric delay, 'Activate drip', student notification controls and saved feedback.

references.title: Community invite screen
references.question: Q2
references.take: Circle's 'Invite members' screen combines selected-space access with admin and moderator permission controls and 'Send invites'. Privilege assignment is separate from choosing spaces.

references.title: Invite and permission dialog
references.question: Q2
references.take: Figma combines email invitation, 'Copy link', existing people and can-view permissions in one dialog. This is a content-sharing pattern that can inform course access.

references.title: Link sharing and password options
references.question: Q2
references.take: Figma shows 'Anyone' access, 'View'/'Edit', optional password protection and a viewers-can-copy/save/export setting before 'Save'. A password is not a classroom join code.

references.title: Creator content manager with Share
references.question: Q2
references.take: Example of what not to do: Gumroad shows a 'Share' tab and 'Collaborators' navigation, but not a learner-access grant or invitation status.

references.title: Page sharing dialog
references.question: Q2
references.take: Notion's 'Add members' pop-up window supports names or emails, an explained 'Member' role, an invitation message and 'Send invite'. Workspace membership is a related pattern, not course enrolment.

references.title: Guest access suggestion
references.question: Q2
references.take: Notion shows a typed email suggestion labelled 'Guest' alongside 'Member' role selection, an invite message and 'Send invite'. Look at identity and role labels together.

references.title: Invite a customer dialog
references.question: Q2
references.take: Podia's 'Invite a customer' pop-up window shows email entry, optional tags, a time-limited access warning, and explicit 'Don't invite'/'Invite customer' actions. This is targeted enrolment evidence, but no role selector or access code or link is visible.

references.title: View as learner flow
references.question: Q3
references.take: This two-step flow explicitly names 'View as learner' and shows the resulting learner-facing screen. It is strong evidence for a low-friction preview entry and a completeness check.

references.title: Preview lesson as enrolled member
references.question: Q3
references.take: This six-step lesson preview flow shows that preview can keep real lesson navigation and content context. Use it as evidence for how complete the preview is, with the learner role label kept visible.

references.title: AI classroom learner preview
references.question: Q3
references.take: Example of what not to treat as a full answer: 'Previewing as a student' and 'Restart preview' are visible for an AI activity. This does not show whole-course or cohort-access preview.

references.title: Curriculum preview in author setup
references.question: Q3
references.take: Example of a narrower preview: 'Curriculum Preview' is visible in the author setup flow. The retained steps do not show the explicit enrolled-member simulation that Circle shows.

references.title: Community space home
references.question: Q4
references.take: This community home is a related course-home pattern: orient the learner with a clear space title and content entry points in the first view. Course progress and next session were not shown.

references.title: Course community home with content feed
references.question: Q4
references.take: This home puts the community or course identity and latest content in the first view. Use it as a related learner-home pattern, with progress and next session needing their own places.

references.title: Learner course home
references.question: Q4
references.take: Coursera puts 'Continue learning', course progress, a module card, 'Resume' and a weekly goal first. Session scheduling and announcements are not shown here.

references.title: Learner course dashboard
references.question: Q4
references.take: Teachable's learner home shows 'Start Lesson', a lesson list and 0% completion, giving the new learner a clear first action.

references.title: Course ready sharing confirmation
references.question: Q5
references.take: Canva's post-publish confirmation says 'Your course is ready', notes team notification, and offers 'Go to Classwork' plus 'Copy link'. That is strong feedback that sharing or publishing succeeded, without pending or accepted learner counts.

references.title: Invite customer to course
references.question: Q5
references.take: Podia's invitation flow shows 'Customer invited', audience rows with progress, and 'Customers'/'Pending' analytics. These screens do not show email delivery, acceptance or course opening.

references.title: Workspace invite management
references.question: Q5
references.take: Slack's invitation management shows 'Requests'/'Pending'/'Accepted'/'Invite Links' tabs plus bounced, resent and revoked invitation states. That gives recovery options beyond a success message.

references.title: Course dashboard on web
references.question: Q6
references.take: Coursera's web home shows enrolled learning, progress, 'Resume' and a weekly goal. Pair it with its iOS example to compare the core learner layout.

references.title: Course dashboard on mobile
references.question: Q6
references.take: Coursera iOS shows module progress, 'Download', daily goals and 'Up Next'. Its matched web screenshot supports layout parity, not proven offline or invite behaviour.

references.title: Learner portal inside admin preview
references.question: Q6
references.take: Teachable shows a learner-facing home inside an 'Edit in Admin' / 'Preview as admin' shell, with Draft lesson labels, 'Start' actions and 0% completion. This is preview context, not an ordinary learner session.

references.title: Course dashboard on mobile
references.question: Q6
references.take: Udemy's iOS learner course home provides mobile context. No matched web screenshot was kept, so web and mobile parity is not shown.
